conservative_sampling_bounds.explanation: Finite-population hypergeometric inversion; each endpoint interval uses Bonferroni across 20 strata. The strict lower and optimistic upper together also give a conservative 95% envelope covering sampling uncertainty plus ambiguity endpoints. Wide bounds are intentional. Coverage concerns the random sample of this saved run, conditional on fixed case judgments, not run-to-run randomness or reviewer validity.

strata.label: unit or subsidiary of
strata.definition: The first organization is an owned subsidiary, division, or organizational unit of the second.
strata.scope_notes: The dominant part/unit/owned-by paths jointly specify organizational containment in the subsidiary-to-parent direction, as in the earlier audit. An acquisition offer alone is insufficient; mere collaboration is excluded.

strata.label: analyst affiliation
strata.definition: The first person works as an analyst for or at the second organization.
strata.scope_notes: Analyst-for/with/at overwhelmingly dominates. Director or partner alone does not establish analyst status. A shared analyst path does not resolve incompatible names within one latent entity.

strata.label: coach of
strata.definition: The first person coaches or coached the second team or institutional sports program.
strata.scope_notes: Coach-of/possessive and active coaching dominate. Historical coaching is included. Considering a vacancy alone, general management, political participation and athletic participation without coaching are excluded.

strata.label: defeated opponent
strata.definition: The first competitor won a contest against the second competitor.
strata.scope_notes: Defeat/victory/sweep form the dominant winning family when grouped; lose-to is the strongest individual competing path and has the opposite direction. Mere participation or a margin/lead without an established victory is excluded. Wins and losses in different historical contests may coexist; one explicit win suffices.

strata.label: director of
strata.definition: The first person is or was a director of the second organization.
strata.scope_notes: The director family clearly dominates the full dictionary, matching the earlier specific-director scope. President/head/chief, analyst, founder or performer alone do not substitute for an explicit directorship. Broader leadership would be an alternative predicate, not an automatic union.

strata.label: chairperson of
strata.definition: The first person is or was chairperson of the second organization.
strata.scope_notes: Chairman noun and possessive paths and chairmanship succession dominate. Historical, resigning or retiring chairpersons are included. The smaller executive/founder family is competing evidence: an executive need not chair the organization. Do not widen this clear office to every managerial role.

strata.label: directed communication
strata.definition: The first person or institution communicates with, requests or urges action from, or advises the second.
strata.scope_notes: Ask/urge/persuade/tell/notify form the coherent dominant communication family used previously. Bare cooperation or replacement is excluded. Send-to without a recoverable communicative object can be ambiguous. Institutional recipients are permitted.

strata.label: chairs or heads organization
strata.definition: The first person holds or held the chair or head leadership office of the second organization or committee.
strata.scope_notes: Chairman/chair and head/lead together dominate the full dictionary. This is an office relationship, not generic membership: member/serve-on/sit-on form a substantial competing family. Historical offices count. Generic political descriptions require a resolved individual; chairmanship of a panel owned by a larger body does not alone establish chairmanship of that larger body.

strata.label: unit or subsidiary of
strata.definition: The first organization is an owned subsidiary, division, or organizational unit of the second.
strata.scope_notes: The dominant unit/subsidiary/owned-by dictionary has the same meaning as rel_250; different learned relation IDs do not require different invented predicates. Membership, speech, employment and completed deal descriptions without containment are not automatically equivalent.

strata.label: economist affiliation
strata.definition: The first person works or worked as an economist for the second organization.
strata.scope_notes: Economist-for/at/of/with dominates, preserving the specific economist scope. President, director, analyst, specialist or forecaster alone is not sufficient. Historical employment counts; unrelated speech attachments remain competing evidence.

strata.label: winner or champion of
strata.definition: The first entity won the competition or award designated by the second, or held its championship title.
strata.scope_notes: Win/champion/victory dominates. Preserve the earlier competition/award scope: historical wins and championship designations qualify, but participation, mere medal receipt without championship, winning an individual stage, and political officeholding do not. Winning the White House is a competing political meaning rather than an expansion of this predicate.

strata.label: director affiliation
strata.definition: The first person holds or held a director role of, for, or at the second organization.
strata.scope_notes: The director family overwhelmingly dominates, consistent with the specific-director scope of rel_263 and earlier reviews. Functional directors employed by an organization are included; this need not mean its sole overall leader. Professor, publisher, speaker, compiler or member alone is excluded. A truncated abstract topic requires identifying the intended institution.

strata.label: executive of
strata.definition: The first person holds or held an executive office in the second organization or governmental jurisdiction.
strata.scope_notes: Executive constructions overwhelmingly dominate. Corporate and county executive offices both qualify under the same office relation. Candidacy, nomination, legislation and being hired by an executive alone do not establish tenure; direct historical titles and resignation do.

strata.label: managerial or leadership office in
strata.definition: The first person holds or held an explicit managerial or leadership office in the second organization or governing body.
strata.scope_notes: The head/chair/executive/chief family collectively dominates and matches the earlier broad managerial-office scope. Include explicit executive, chair, president, director or equivalent office without requiring sole overall control. Analyst, founder, owner, ordinary employment and a nomination alone are excluded.

strata.label: president or manager of
strata.definition: The first person holds or held an explicitly identified president or manager office in the second organization, team or public body.
strata.scope_notes: The president family dominates, with a smaller manager family. Preserve the earlier president-or-manager scope. Generic head, chair, executive, director, coach, athlete or ordinary employment alone is insufficient. Functional presidential roles within an organization count without claiming sole chief presidency; modifiers missing from a path cannot be reconstructed.

strata.label: political or organizational leader of
strata.definition: The first person is or was a political, organizational or community leader of the group, legislature or political body designated by the second argument.
strata.scope_notes: Leader-of/noun/possessive dominates. Preserve the earlier political-group scope, including legislative majority/minority leadership and adjectival group names when direct leadership paths establish the group connection. A generic political label is not a uniquely named person; incompatible personal names remain identity ambiguities. Do not infer formal state control from spiritual/community leadership or mere founding.

strata.label: winner or champion of
strata.definition: The first entity won the competition or award designated by the second, or held its championship title.
strata.scope_notes: Win and winner dominate, using the same scope as rel_112 and the earlier reviews. Reaching or participating in an event, winning only a stage, and winning political office do not establish this competition/award predicate. A malformed appended path is not needed when clean direct evidence exists.

strata.label: defeated opponent
strata.definition: The first competitor won a contest against the second competitor.
strata.scope_notes: Beat/defeat/victory dominates, preserving the directed defeated-opponent scope used in rel_114 and earlier audits. Mere play, trade, contract or political/geographical comparison is insufficient. Historical wins and losses can coexist, but ambiguous competitors must still be resolved.

strata.label: geographical part of
strata.definition: The first named neighborhood, district or area is geographically contained in the second place.
strata.scope_notes: Area/section/neighborhood-of/in strongly dominates. This is a place-to-containing-place relationship, distinct from personal residence, travel, schools or an organization located somewhere. The listed longer paths may be noisy without invalidating clean containment evidence; incompatible neighborhood names require identity review.

strata.label: owner of
strata.definition: The first person or organization owns or owned the second property, company, network or team.
strata.scope_notes: Owner/own and corporate parent paths dominate in the owner-to-property direction, matching the earlier ownership scope. Historical ownership counts. Merger, rejected acquisition, chairmanship of an owner, publishing or a bare possessive alone does not establish ownership.
